what_matters.head: Chip and AI stocks fell on Thursday after the Financial Times reported that OpenAI's annualised revenue was about $50 billion at the end of September, not the $68 billion widely reported late last month.
what_matters.detail: CNBC confirmed that OpenAI gave investors the $50 billion figure. A person familiar with it told CNBC the $68 billion figure counted OpenAI's partners' gross revenue, to compare it with Anthropic. The chip-stock fund SOXX fell 3.4% and the Nasdaq Composite 1.3%, while the S&P 500 lost 0.5% and the Dow rose 0.1%. Nvidia, Broadcom, CoreWeave and Micron were among the names that fell (see Movers).

what_matters.head: TSMC's third-quarter sales came to NT$1.49 trillion, about US$46.7 billion, above its own US$44.6–45.8 billion forecast and the analysts' NT$1.46 trillion (LSEG).
what_matters.detail: September alone was up 54.6% on a year earlier. January–September sales grew 41.1%, up from 39.3% for January–August. The figures came out at 13:30 SGT Thursday, before the US session; TSMC's US shares still fell 3.0% that day. Full results, with the gross margin and next quarter's forecast, come on 15 Oct.

what_matters.head: WeRide's US shares fell 9.1%, three times their usual daily swing, on almost twice their average volume. No reported cause found.
what_matters.detail: The shares have lost 22.5% over the past month. The latest dated report found on the company is a Bloomberg Intelligence note from 2 Oct saying China's robotaxi operators face losses through 2028; nothing from Thursday's session.

latest.tape_note: The S&P 500 and the Nasdaq fell for a second day, led by chip and AI stocks (see What matters). Treasury yields eased after a solid 30-year bond auction: the 10-year closed 5bp lower at 5.23%. Oil jumped: WTI rose 3.6% to $91.49 and Brent 4.1% to $104.28. Reuters said Iranian attacks on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz last week were the most since the war began, and Hurricane Isaias shut in part of US Gulf of Mexico oil output. Prices came off their highs after Trump said he would not attack Iran before the 3 Nov US midterm elections. Gold rose 0.4%; the US dollar was flat against the Singapore dollar (+0.06%).
latest.tonight: No high-impact US release on the calendar tonight. Micron's board meeting runs through Friday US time, and its Taoyuan union expects an answer on profit-sharing. Korea's market is shut today.
